newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent holds London gains, gasoline higher.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent holds London gains, gasoline higher.

text.p: September Brent futures were untraded but were holding London levels in Asia at midday on Thursday and NYMEX gasoline marched higher on a squeeze in the U.S. market.
NYMEX August gasoline, which expires later on Thursday, was last traded on ACCESS at 70.50 cents per gallon, for a gain of 0.60 cents from New York.
The contract gained 3.43 cents in New York on worries over tight supplies. Product is delivered against long positions at settlement.
The gasoline market kept crude supported and London September Brent rose 38 to $18.97 per barrel, while NYMEX September Brent rose in New York 45 to $20.30.
The NYMEX September crude added a further six cents on ACCESS to last trade at $20.36 per barrel.
September Brent on SIMEX was bid at $19.00 after London settled at $18.97.

The U.S. Energy Information Administration said on Wednesday that U.S. reformulated gasoline stocks -- delivered against the NYMEX contract -- fell 3.5 million barrels last week, confirming an earlier API report that showed a decline of 3.2 million.
But brokers said the expiry of the gasoline contract later on Thursday will ease the upward pressure, while crude was wary of a flood of Iraqi oil if Baghdad resumes oil exports in coming weeks.
